hayai-relay: message::tests::truncation_never_decodes fails on both backends (proptest counterexample saved 2026-10-04 16:44 in proptest-regressions/message.txt: a truncated CompactBlock decodes). Found by W4 gate; not caused by W4 files
notes: Cause (coordinator analysis): the v2 CompactBlock marks its full-id section by presence at the end of the payload ('a frame that ends after prefilled is the v1 layout'). A payload cut exactly before that section is a valid v1 payload, so decode_payload accepts it. The outer frame length and the legacy checksum catch real truncation, but the payload format is ambiguous. Root fix: give the v2 layout its own message type code (payload always has the full-id count, zero allowed), so presence is never inferred from the end of the payload. Touches hayai-relay message.rs/compact.rs, hayai-net relay.rs (send by negotiated version), docs/protocol-compact-relay.md, the ZIP. Do after W5 finishes (it owns hayai-net now).

title: hayai-bench: concurrent fixture generation races on the cache file (CI cold cache fails)
description: store_cached in crates/hayai-bench/src/fixtures.rs writes <name>.bin.tmp and renames it. With an empty bench-fixtures/ (every fresh CI runner), several tests generate the same fixture in parallel: they share one tmp path, the first rename moves it and the others panic with 'rename fixture file: NotFound' (fixtures.rs:520). Seen in a cold run of cargo test --workspace --release: 5 hayai-bench lib tests fail upstream, 1 on zakura; a warm run passes. Use a unique tmp name per writer (pid and thread id, or tempfile in the same directory) so the atomic rename makes the last writer win, or generate each fixture once behind a lock. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, test job) fails on a cold fixture cache until then, and actions/cache saves the cache only after a green job.

title: M3: sans-IO relay policy
description: hayai-net/src/relay.rs mixes relay decisions with sockets, threads and mutexes. Move the policy into a state machine (events in, messages out); hayai-net keeps the I/O.
notes:
Assessment 2026-10-08 (macOS session). hayai-net/src/relay.rs: 2,966 lines, 95 lock sites over 15 Mutex fields (peers, lanes, batches, candidates, recent blocks, pending compact blocks, unannounced, mempool polls, ...), one reader thread per peer calls Relay::on_message concurrently. The handshake and ping policy is already sans-IO (session.rs: PeerSession::on_message/on_tick -> Vec<Action>, 10 unit tests). The rest is the policy: on_inv/on_getdata/on_tx_bytes/on_block_bytes/on_compact/candidates/batches/pending retries. Plan: (1) RelayPolicy state machine in hayai-relay or a new hayai-net::policy: events in (peer joined/left, message from peer, block found, block validated, tx announced, tick(now)), actions out (send legacy/compact to peer, to all of an audience, ingest tx/block to the sinks, sync event, disconnect, misbehaved). The stores stay behind the TxLookup/ChainSource/HeaderCheck traits as inputs. (2) hayai-net keeps sockets, threads, the per-peer writers, and one policy lock. Risk: one lock in place of 15 serializes the reader threads; the relay bench forward_latency and the M13 counters decide, and a sharded policy (per-peer state out of the global lock) is the fallback. Needs the Linux machine: hayai-net/tests/peers.rs binds 127.0.0.x (fails on macOS) and the gate needs perf counters.
2026-10-08: done as policy.rs (RelayPolicy + Io trait) and relay.rs (shell). Same locks, same handler bodies; 3 recording-Io tests. Relay bench before/after pending (worktree hayai-m3base at HEAD + perf-event gate for the baseline).
close_reason: RelayPolicy (policy.rs, sans-socket, Io trait) + Relay shell (relay.rs). Same locks and handler bodies; 3 recording-Io tests; loopback 24 pass.

title: M2: contextual consensus rules out of hayai-state
description: Move the contextual rules of hayai-state/src/check.rs into hayai-consensus-core (M12) as pure functions over shell-resolved facts; hayai-state keeps the reads and builds the facts.
notes:
Hand-off 2026-10-08 (stage 2 of the consensus core; no file of stage 2 exists yet). Stage 1 (M12) is in the tree: hayai-consensus-core with spec, rules, limits, subsidy, funding, lockbox, founders, nsm, difficulty, header, coinbase_value; hayai-consensus is the adapter. Stage 2 design, agreed with the formal-verification session:
1. Remove #![no_std] and extern crate alloc from hayai-consensus-core/src/lib.rs (owner rule: no_std is never a goal).
2. New module block: BlockContext (shell-resolved coins of the inputs, nullifier and anchor presence, parent value pools, history state, difficulty context), TxFacts (plain per-transaction facts, borrowed, not zcash_primitives::Transaction), Delta, and the stage-2 RuleError.
3. check_block(spec, rules, ctx, txs) -> Result<Delta, RuleError>, then a verdict step that takes the script and proof flags. hayai-state keeps the reads and builds the facts; hayai-validate keeps rayon and batching.
4. One RuleError variant for each rule, named after its row in docs/consensus.md, with the row name in the doc comment. Split a ContextError that covers several rows. Error enums stay flat.
5. In-block uniqueness of nullifiers and outpoints: the shell sorts; the core checks in one pass that the input is sorted and has no duplicate (no set type, no trusted sort).
6. Same Aeneas subset as stage 1 (tests/subset.rs): index loops, no iterator adapters, no HashMap/HashSet/BTreeMap, no closures that capture &mut, no break/continue/return out of a nested loop, no &mut as a generic argument, checked money arithmetic with typed errors, try_from instead of as, no unwrap/expect/assert/unreachable/panic, no failing index. Move the i128 sums of hayai-state/src/check.rs (about lines 586-587, 709-731) into checked core arithmetic.
7. validate_block, commit_prebuilt and the restart replay call the same core functions. apply_checkpointed calls the same delta function but runs no rule function (checkpoint trust, as Zebra and Zakura); owner decision pending: the proof takes the checkpoint list as an axiom (recommended) or the node checks these blocks.
8. Measure the validation benchmarks before and after (stage 1: instruction counts equal to 0.1 %, time per block within 1 %).
2026-10-08 owner: no formal verification work for now. Checkpoint decision when resumed: the proof takes the checkpoint list as an axiom (option 1).

hayai-node: the block source as a trait (relay/sync or upstream follower)
description: Follow-up of M1 (hayai-341). Shadow mode is in hayai-node by Config ([shadow]): Node::start branches on Mode for the upstream follower, UpstreamBacking and the seed. Make the block source a trait that NodeBuilder takes: the relay with the sync (full mode), the upstream follower (shadow mode), or a source of the caller. The relay transport is the second injection point: hayai_net::policy::RelayPolicy with an Io of the caller in place of the TCP shell. Needs sync_tests on Linux.

title: Full mode: the HeaderChain as the relay's HeaderContext; drop the index window
description: Follow-up of M4 (hayai-vfx). In full mode HeaderChain and hayai_sync::index::HeaderIndex are two structures linked by commit order (node.rs finish_commit: index.push then sync.committed -> mark_body_valid; disconnect_to: index.pop). The relay's check reads the index, so a relayed block whose parent is a header-only chain entry is ParentUnknown -> BlockInv, and a relayed block is checked twice (relay ingest, then Sync::relayed). Design: impl HeaderContext for HeaderChain (has_block = lookup; parent = Dag::ancestors walk; status-aware), the index stays for shadow mode (seed start) or the chain gets a seed root. Needs the node network tests (sync_tests, 127.0.0.x) on Linux and the M13 gate.
